concept.title: How Hard is it?
concept.shortdesc: How difficult is it to build a desktop PC?

conbody.p: Building a desktop is not as complex as it might seem at first. Most parts and cables snap together with a little pressure or only require a few screws to hold in place. Connectors are generally clearly labeled and designed to only go together one way, making it difficult to go wrong during assembly. It’s not substantially more difficult than assembling a LEGO set or building an IKEA bookshelf, although the specter of financial risk when placing a $200 processor into a $100 motherboard can make it feel like more of an ordeal.

The most difficult part of building a desktop is not the labor required to put everything together, but the planning that goes into selecting parts. The number of possible components and configurations can very easily seem overwhelming. The reader needs the ability to gauge their own needs, set a budget, do basic internet research, handle simple tools, and follow basic directions.
